children: Wall Street's major market averages finished well in the red on Wednesday, as investors received the latest rate hike decision from the FOMC.
The blue-chip Dow
ended -1.2%, the benchmark S&P 500 (
) closed -0.4%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite
ended near even.
From a sector-by-sector vantage point, eight of the 11 segments finished to the downside, with energy being the weakest performer.
The Federal Open Market Committee increased its benchmark interest rate by
on Wednesday, as widely expected, the first rate hike in more than three years.

“According to Kevin Warsh, the new Chairman of the Federal Reserve, ‘The plain fact is that inflation is too high, and has been for too long’. There has been no sign, according to him, that underlying trends have improved meaningfully. This comes as inflationary pressures continue to be problematic. Diesel prices, for instance, hit an all-time high in the last week. This can be attributed largely to the war against Iran. But in general, inflation has been running hotter for a while now,” Seeking Alpha analyst
noted.

“Wednesday's rate hike sends a message to the markets that the Federal Reserve isn't just talking about inflation, it's actually doing something about it. While one 25-basis point hike isn't likely to bring inflation down overnight, it could help to stabilize the bond market, which has a direct impact on borrowing costs," Alex Guiliano of Resonate Wealth Partners stated.

Elsewhere on the economic front, export prices unexpectedly rose in August, while the import prices increased more than expected. Moreover, the retail sales rebounded in August, coming in better than expected.
The U.S. 2-Year Treasury yield
climbed 7 basis points to 4.74%, the U.S. 10-Year Treasury yield
ticked up by 1 basis point to 5.01%, and the U.S. 30-Year Treasury yield
pushed lower by 1 basis point to 5.35%.
